session: This round was opened by the SESSION as M0-c-04's HARDENING ROUND S8 (J237 (2): the M0 hardening phase's fix rounds, batched per owning item; J238: M0 is the bedrock — the default for an M0 row is FIX with an exact precaution and a pin; J567: the bar is an independent closing check's PASS on the evidence), on THE CONTRACTS ROUND's consumer row for RL15 (queue Q135; this item's N-10 of round S4, REPORTED as a contract between items; J803 R3, R8, R10): S5a's gate plan made by the kernel's dry run instead of a batch that is always rejected. Each 'failing line' below is one such row — an open queue row routed to this item (docs/M0-FIX-QUEUE.md) or a row the item's latest closing check wrote into its notes file; its evidence names the SOURCE you MUST read whole before fixing; the fix shape and the pin are the session's reading, binding unless the source or the code shows it wrong — then say so in your notes and do what the finding needs. THE RULES OF A HARDENING ROUND: (1) inside the item's owns and nowhere else — a row that needs another item's file is REPORTED, not built; (2) every row gets a PIN (a test that is red without the fix; your mutant table shows each pin killing its mutant) unless the row is comment-only or asks for a choices row — then the text is the deliverable; (3) BEHAVIOUR: a hardening fix may move output where a defect is fixed — a DECLARED shift, stated in your choices row with the before and after (digests and goldens re-recorded in the same round, named), never silent; where a row offers alternatives, take the one the design's text supports and say which; a change of an operation's or stage's CONTRACT (its design-level behaviour, a record or file format, an exported API) is NOT yours — report it as a note for the session's ruling and leave the row at REPORTED; (4) J264 / N-58: the refusal census of the item's registered families before and after the round, never rising (a row whose fix makes a lawful input succeed lowers it and says so); (5) API frozen (J263 Q1): no export of a folder index or the barrel added, removed or renamed unless a row explicitly asks for one — then the index change is the row's and stated; message texts pinned verbatim where a row changes one (J263 Q6); (6) the gates, NEAR and RELATED@1000 as the brief above says, at W=1; (7) the item's notes file gains a section 'Hardening round S8' with the row-by-row outcome (fixed / pinned / reported, each with its evidence and mutant), and the round's choices row names every row it closes. The CLOSING CHECKER confirms every row's outcome with its own evidence (re-reading the source note or queue row), re-kills every pin's mutant, re-measures the refusal census, and judges new findings by the blocker rule only; a row left REPORTED with a stated contract reason is not a failing line. THIS IS LEG 3 OF A MERGED ROUND OF THREE LEGS — THE CONTRACTS ROUND, M0-a-06's (the MERGED-ROUND RULE, J443; J803 R1, R2): M0-a-06 S11 → M0-e-03 S6 → M0-c-04 S8, in that order, on ONE tree and ONE branch, no reset between, each leg with its own build, closing check, LANDED line and record; EACH LEG LAUNCHES ONLY IF THE LEG BEFORE IT PASSED (ok with check.verdict pass) — legs 2 and 3 share no file, but @plat/layout depends on @plat/site, so a failed leg 2 must never sit under leg 3's gates: a failure HANDS BACK, and the session launches what is left. Legs 2 and 3 also wait on the landings of the rounds now in flight on their items (M0-e-03 S5, child EA; M0-c-04 S7, child EC). The round carries no leg of M0-a-05: the refusal that names a body is made by the transaction at commit (kernel/src/tx/tx.ts roleProblems → run → reject), and a plan that commits nothing for a SEQUENCE of splits is a dry run, which only tx/ can open and undo (docs/validation/a05-contracts-spec-2026-11-13/draft.md §0, §1.1, §1.3 (c)). Its neighbour: Q181's round is M0-a-06 S12 (J803 R1; its drafted entry docs/validation/q181-ruling-2026-11-12/spec-a06-s11.json keeps its file name), specced on the head that holds this round's leg 1 and the RQ2 round's third leg; it lands after this round and re-takes its own baselines there. THE RESTARTS (a fact of this platform on 2026-11-12 / 13: a container restarts about every two hours whether or not background tasks are live; /home/user/maps-scratch survives, every process dies, /tmp does not survive): every run over ten minutes is a STEP OF A RE-ENTRANT CHAIN under /home/user/maps-scratch/waves/ — its log and its exit-code file beside it, and for a run of many parts one exit-code file per part, so that a seat that comes back after a restart skips what is finished: the census one file per seed or family; RELATED@1000 IN CHUNKS — collect RELATED's own file list once (`vitest related --run` with the JSON reporter and a test-name filter that matches nothing, e.g. -t '^__no_such_test__$'), split it by 12 files, run each chunk with `vitest run --passWithNoTests` at PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=1000 under ONE recorded PLAT_FUZZ_SEED, each chunk's JSON report and exit code beside it, the totals summed from the JSON reports (a file that registers no test at 1 000 runs is named); NEAR one run per project; each mutant its own exit-code file. A CHECKPOINT line names the chain's directory and its next unfinished step at least every twenty minutes of the seat's own work. No timing bar is judged on these machines. THE SEATS: the session's tiers for a stage item (J390 / J631 / J714), named at launch; the CLOSING CHECK is the STRONGER checker's — this leg changes SOURCE. THE WAITING RULE and the waiter as the brief above says. LEG 3's OWN TEXT.
